selection.why: Round3 is better on median and mean case span, waiting, and service, with every directional change significant and none significantly worse. It also removes CA-002, whose attributable contribution worsened activity by 1.572 h per case, while retaining the strong reductions from AE-002 and SPC-003.
selection.gain_reading: both: waiting h/case is down 64.108% and service h/case is down 88.516%, so cases queue less and the redesigned process also performs substantially less work. Absolute case-span hours are not provided in the payload; the attributed activity-hour net is -9.9068 h/case, which is not comparable with the case-span measures.

selection.runner_up: round2c — it retains the same broad redesign but costs 2.524 percentage points on median case span, 1.383 points on waiting, and 2.374 points on service, while also retaining the harmful CA-002 assignment change.
selection.caveat: Do not read the headline reductions as purely faster work: service falls 88.516%, meaning substantially less work is being done, and 485 cases per run end at different outcomes. The measures do not establish whether those changed outcomes are desirable, and utilisation has no directional interpretation.

note: `best` is the best MEASUREMENT in the run, which is usually not the last round. ⚠️ `statistically_tied_with_best` is the SELECTOR'S CANDIDATE POOL, not a set of indistinguishable results: a row is admitted either because it is not significantly worse than `best` on the median, or because it is decisively better on ONE directional measure while possibly far worse on the others. Read each row's `admitted_because` before describing it, and never call the list a tie. `per_candidate` is the winning plan's own account: what each surviving candidate contributed on waiting, duration, throughput and resources.
